excerpt: Kenya safari holidays from the UK, planned in order: how many days to book, which school holidays work, Heathrow flights, the eTA and new insurance rule, and real Divulge prices.
content:
Kenya safari holidays from the UK usually run 7 to 10 days: an overnight nonstop flight from Heathrow to Nairobi, then a private 4x4 safari through Amboseli, the Rift Valley lakes and the Masai Mara, often with a few nights on the Indian Ocean at the end. Our private week starts from US$2,711 per adult before flights.

Planning Kenya safari holidays from Britain raises the same questions every time: how many nights, which school holiday, what the dollar prices mean in pounds, and what changed on entry rules this year. This guide answers them in order, using the real itineraries behind our Kenya safari packages and the official UK advice you should read before booking.

Quick Facts

  • Typical length: 7-10 days on the ground, plus an overnight flight each way
  • Flights: nonstop Heathrow to Nairobi with British Airways and Kenya Airways, about 9 hours (checked November 2026)
  • Time difference: Kenya is 3 hours ahead of the UK in winter, 2 in summer
  • Entry: Kenya eTA from US$30, plus Kenyan Government travel health insurance since October 2026
  • Prices: Divulge safaris start from US$880 (4 days, shared) to US$3,015 (10 days, private), per adult
  • Busiest UK dates: August, Christmas and Easter, when safari prices rise
  • Malaria: risk across most of Kenya outside Nairobi city; ask your GP or travel clinic about tablets

What Does a Kenya Safari Holiday Look Like?

Kenya safari holidays are road or fly-in tours between national parks and reserves, with a driver-guide, game drives morning and afternoon, and full-board lodges or tented camps. Most UK visitors land in Nairobi and head straight out on the classic southern circuit.

Most Kenya safari holidays on that circuit link three very different landscapes. Amboseli has elephants below Kilimanjaro, the Rift Valley lakes add rhinos, flamingos and a boat ride among hippos, and the Masai Mara brings big cats and, from about July to October, the wildebeest migration. Our 7-day Kenya safari itinerary maps it day by day.

On a private safari the 4x4 Land Cruiser and guide are yours, so you can sit with a lion pride for an hour or head back for lunch; a shared safari mixes you with other travellers to cut the cost. Private vehicles are the norm on Kenya safari holidays, not a luxury add-on.

How Many Days Should a Kenya Safari Holiday Last?

Seven days on the ground is the sweet spot for Kenya safari holidays booked from the UK. It fits three parks without long drives every day and works with a nine-night block of annual leave once the overnight flights are added. Shorter trips suit the Mara only; longer ones slow the pace or add the beach.

Seven days: the classic first safari

A week covers Amboseli, the lakes and three nights in the Mara. Drives between parks take three to six hours, broken by game viewing on the way, and the final day ends in Nairobi in time for an evening flight to London. Most of the Kenya safari holidays we plan for UK couples follow this shape.

Ten days or more: room to breathe

Ten days lets you start gently around Nairobi with the elephant orphanage and the Giraffe Centre, add Hell's Gate on foot or by bicycle, and spend full days in each park. It is also the length to choose for Kenya safari holidays that end on the coast.

How Much Do Kenya Safari Holidays Cost for UK Travellers?

Kenya safari holidays are priced per adult sharing, almost always in US dollars, ours included. Expect about US$880 for a shared 4-day trip, US$2,700-3,000 for a private week or 10 days in mid-range lodges, and more for fly-in conservancy camps.

Paying in dollars from a sterling account

Because Kenya safari holidays are quoted in dollars, the pound's exchange rate on the day you pay decides what the trip costs you in sterling. If the rate matters to you, ask your bank about a currency account or fixing a rate before the balance is due.

Why August and Christmas cost more

Our trip pages note that prices rise over Christmas, Easter and in August, exactly when UK schools break up and Kenya safari holidays are most in demand. Travel in late January, February or early March and the same itinerary often costs less. Our Kenya safari cost guide breaks the daily rate down by lodge tier.

Which UK School Holidays Suit a Kenya Safari?

The UK summer holidays suit Kenya safari holidays best, because August is dry season and the migration is usually in the Masai Mara. February half-term is the quieter alternative, while Easter and May half-term fall in the long rains, with greener, emptier parks.

For month-by-month weather and wildlife, see our best time to visit Kenya guide.

Booking Kenya safari holidays for the school summer break

If you are tied to August, book flights and Mara lodges together, ideally nine to twelve months out, because the camps nearest the river fill first. Families with younger children often prefer a private vehicle so the day can bend around naps and snacks; our family safari planning guide covers minimum ages and room types.

How Do You Fly From London to Nairobi?

London Heathrow has nonstop flights to Nairobi's Jomo Kenyatta International Airport with British Airways and Kenya Airways, and the fastest take about 9 hours (route schedules checked November 2026). Evening departures arrive the next morning, so Kenya safari holidays can start on landing day.

From Manchester, Edinburgh or Dublin, most travellers connect through Heathrow or a European or Gulf hub; compare total journey time, not only the fare, as a long layover can cost you a day in the bush. With Kenya only two or three hours ahead of the UK, jet lag is mild.

A late arrival simply means a first night in Nairobi. Hops between parks or to the coast use short flights from Wilson Airport; our fly-in safari packages show the routes.

Kenya Safari Holidays With a Beach Finish

Adding the coast is the most popular way UK travellers extend a Kenya safari, and the two halves suit each other: early starts and dust in the bush, then three or four nights of doing very little by the Indian Ocean. The main choice is which beach and how you get there.

The route with no backtracking is Tsavo to Watamu: drive from Nairobi through Tsavo West and Tsavo East, then straight down to the coast for snorkelling in Watamu Marine National Park, Mida Creek and the Gede Ruins, then fly from Malindi to Nairobi. The other option is the Mara first, then a flight to Diani, south of Mombasa. Our bush and beach safaris page and the Diani Beach guide compare the two coasts.

What Should You Check Before Booking: Entry, Health and Safety?

British passport holders booking Kenya safari holidays need an eTA, a passport valid for six months after arrival with two blank pages, and, since October 2026, Kenyan Government travel health insurance bought during the eTA application. The FCDO recommends applying at least two weeks before you travel (FCDO Kenya entry requirements, checked November 2026).

The new travel health insurance

The FCDO says the Kenyan Government cover is bought inside the eTA application and that foreign policies are not accepted in its place for this requirement. Keep your own UK travel insurance too, covering cancellation and medical evacuation. Our Kenya eTA guide walks through the form, and the Flying Doctors cover page explains evacuation from remote parks.

Malaria and vaccines

UK travel health guidance rates malaria risk as high across most of Kenya, including safari areas and the coast, and low in Nairobi city (NHS Fit for Travel Kenya; the current UK source is TravelHealthPro, both checked November 2026). See your GP or a travel clinic six to eight weeks before flying. A yellow fever certificate is needed only if you arrive from a country with transmission risk. Our Kenya safari vaccinations post lists the usual jabs.

Is the FCDO advising against the safari areas?

No. The FCDO travel advice for Kenya (checked November 2026) advises against travel to parts of the north-east and the far north coast near the Somali border, such as Mandera, Garissa and most of Lamu County outside Lamu and Manda islands. The places visited on most Kenya safari holidays, including the Masai Mara, Amboseli, Tsavo, Nairobi, Diani and Watamu, are not on that list. Our Kenya safari safety guide covers everyday precautions.

Insider Tips

  • Book the Mara first: in August the camps nearest the river fill before flights do, so secure them, then book London to Nairobi
  • Use the overnight flight: an evening Heathrow departure lands in the morning, so you lose no safari day
  • Bring small dollar notes: tips and drinks are easier in clean, newer US dollar notes
  • Check the plug: Kenya uses the same three-pin Type G plug as the UK, so no adaptor is needed

Frequently Asked Questions

How long should a Kenya safari holiday be?

A Kenya safari holiday of 7 days suits most UK travellers: it covers Amboseli, the Rift Valley lakes and three nights in the Masai Mara without rushing. Four days works for the Mara alone on a tight budget, and 10 days adds Nairobi, Hell's Gate and slower travel, or a few nights on the coast at the end.

How much does a Kenya safari holiday cost from the UK?

Kenya safari holidays with Divulge start from about US$880 per adult for a 4-day shared budget trip, US$2,711 for a private 7-day safari and US$3,015 for 10 days, in low season. UK travellers then add return flights from London, the US$30 Kenya eTA, travel insurance and tips of about US$10 per person per day.

Is there a direct flight from London to Nairobi?

Yes. British Airways and Kenya Airways both fly nonstop from London Heathrow to Nairobi, and the fastest flights take about 9 hours. Overnight departures land in Nairobi the next morning, which lets most Kenya safari holidays start the same day with a drive to Amboseli or the Masai Mara.

Do British citizens need a visa for Kenya?

British citizens do not need a traditional visa but must get a Kenya Electronic Travel Authorisation before flying. The eTA starts at US$30, the FCDO suggests applying at least two weeks ahead, and your passport needs six months of validity and two blank pages. Since October 2026 most visitors must also buy Kenyan Government travel health insurance during the application.

When is the best time for a Kenya safari holiday with children from the UK?

For Kenya safari holidays with children, the UK summer holidays work best: they fall in Kenya's dry season and the Great Migration usually reaches the Masai Mara between July and October, so August is the classic family choice. It is also peak season, so book early. February half-term is a quieter, drier alternative with lower prices and good game viewing.

Final Thoughts

The best Kenya safari holidays from the UK start with the length, then the month: a week for a first visit, ten days for the coast or a slower pace, and August or February half-term depending on migration or price. Sort the eTA and insurance early, then send us your dates for our Kenya safaris.
